crude.up_what: Importer currencies tend to weaken against the dollar, and exporter currencies tend to firm.
crude.up_view: List the foreign-currency payments you owe on imports that are not yet hedged, and check that your current hedges match the amounts and dates of the next payment cycle.
crude.down_what: Importer currencies tend to firm against the dollar, and exporter currencies tend to ease.
crude.down_view: Do not close out hedges because of one price move; first test whether your hedged share of each exposure still fits the updated forecast.

crude.up_what: Higher crude lifts headline inflation, which can keep central banks tighter for longer.
crude.up_view: Before the next central-bank decisions, calculate floating-rate interest cost under a scenario where interest rates stay high for longer than expected.
crude.down_what: Lower crude eases headline inflation and can give central banks room to pause.
crude.down_view: Confirm that your plans to borrow at a fixed rate are unchanged; one price move does not show where central banks will set interest rates.

crude.up_what: Fuel and input costs rise, so cash tied up in inventory and receivables grows.
crude.up_view: Confirm that your committed credit lines are large enough for the bigger swing in working capital, and calculate what drawing on them would cost at current short-term interest rates.
crude.down_what: Working-capital needs ease, and released cash sits in short-term deposits.
crude.down_view: Update the cash forecast first, then invest any cash that is freed up within the investment policy's limits on maturity and counterparty.

crude.up_what: Commodity hedges settle daily, so on positions that lose when prices rise, a sharp move can call for cash within a day.
crude.up_view: Check that the cash you hold to meet variation margin calls (daily top-up payments on hedging contracts) is enough, and who is authorised to approve a same-day transfer.
crude.down_what: On positions that lose when prices fall, the margin call comes on the way down instead.
crude.down_view: Identify which hedges lose value if the price falls, and confirm that your cash buffer for margin calls and your same-day approval process can still cope.

crude.up_what: Energy-heavy customers and suppliers come under pressure, while producers' credit tends to improve.
crude.up_view: Rank your counterparties again by how much their business depends on energy prices, and review credit limits for those you give long payment terms.
crude.down_what: Producers come under pressure, while energy-heavy users get relief.
crude.down_view: Rank your counterparties again, starting with energy producers, and review credit limits for those you give long payment terms.

points.head: Qatar money markets
points.text: QCB raised its deposit, repo and lending rates by 25 bp each from 17 September, to 4.10%, 4.35% and 4.60%. The deposit rate now sits above both SOFR (3.88%) and the top of the Fed range (4.00%), with the riyal pegged at QAR 3.64 per USD.
points.view: Before placing surplus cash, compare riyal deposit yields with dollar deposit yields for the same maturity, and keep counterparty limits unchanged while yields rise.
